note: Triennial election of Tyrone County Council, 1955. Nominations closed on 17 May 1955; the Ulster Herald reports 'THERE will be no contests for Tyrone County Council seats' and lists the members of the new council division by division (Ulster Herald, 21 May 1955, p. 9). The five changes are Castlecaulfield (Steen for Cuddy), Castlederg (Robinson for Gamble), Clogher (Smith for Stewart), Cookstown (McConnell for Glasgow) and Pomeroy (Devlin for Hagan). The list prints no party labels; the paper states the council is 15 Unionists and 12 Nationalists. No poll took place; the round keeps the queue's statutory date, Thursday 2 June 1955, which no retrieved page states. Uncontested divisions here reflect a deliberate abstention, not missing coverage: in the Omagh Rural District, Nationalists refused to nominate against Unionist-held seats in every year except 1949, when only 4 of 21 such seats were contested (Kingsley 2021, 'The Omagh Rural District Electoral Divisions Scheme 1923', citing PRONI LA/62/2/FA/38 and Ulster Herald 10 Feb 1923). The same pattern is visible across this county's rounds. See notes/tyrone-county-council_absent_contests.txt Returned unopposed.
